principles.text: Validate before building: get 100 waitlist signups, offer a 90% off presale, and build the MVP only after five sales.
Start SEO from day one; it compounds and also validates that you can drive traffic to the product.
Product beats distribution: if the product isn't doing well, the product is the problem, not the marketing.
In B2B, start paid and price around $49; free tiers attract the wrong crowd and irrelevant feedback.
Stay lean: founders do the work until traction, split 50/50 with a co-maker, and hire no one before about $50k MRR.

sampleQA.question: How do I validate a SaaS idea before writing code?

answer.text: Launch a waitlist and see if you can reach 100 signups, then email them a 90% off presale. Five sales means you build the first MVP.
If fewer than 10% of your waitlist pays when you ask, it won't get easier after launch.
Deliver the job manually for about 10 paying people first; changing your own routine is easier than changing code.

sampleQA.question: Which growth channels should a bootstrapped founder focus on?

answer.text: His split is roughly 30% SEO, 30% cross-promotion across his own products, 30% build-in-public social, 10% other.
For Unicorn Platform, directories, SEO, Reddit, LinkedIn and affiliates worked; ads, cold email, giveaways and lifetime deals failed.
Be generous with affiliates: moving from 15% to 33% made his program pick up, and he suggests up to 50% if costs are low.
Focus on one social platform until 4-5k followers, then expand everywhere.

sampleQA.question: How do I pick a directory niche that can rank?

answer.text: About 80% of a directory's success is keyword research and domain, 15% data quality, 5% technology.
Find a high-traffic keyword with no directory on Google's first page; check volume in Keyword Planner and competition with a Google search.
Buy a .com, launch from a template in under an hour, and let the domain warm up before publishing the blog.
Monetize with featured spots, sponsors and affiliate links, and use directories to send traffic to your SaaS tools.
